caption:

If you are planning a trip to this amazing part of the USA, make sure to follow @peekinourjournal and see more bucketlist spots and destinations to have the best time out here ❤️

↩️ Arches National Park- One of the most famous national parks in the country. It boasts amazing natural arches, including Delicate Arch which is Utah’s License Plate Symbol
♦️ Canyonlands National Park- Spectacular park with amazing views! Catching the sunrise at Mesa Arch when it glows red, has to be on your list
🐎 Dead Horse Point State Park- One of the best sunrise spots in Moab, this state park deserves so much more love! The entry fee is $20 and we highly recommend visiting this place on your trip to Moab
🛻 Marlboro Point- This hidden gem is only accessible via a 4x4 vehicle and offers jaw dropping views across deep, rugged canyons
🏜️ Goblin Valley State Park- Red rocks and rugged hoodoos dominate the landscape of this beautiful park. You can purchase a drone permit at the entrance station 
👽 Bentonite Hills- Located near Mars Research station, this otherworldly spot will surely make you feel like you transported to another planet
🏰 Capitol Reef National Park- The least visited National Park in Utah, this destination is a hidden gem.There are stunning views everywhere and park offers some amazing hikes and even world class rappelling!
🪨 Factory Butte- This beautiful monolith overlooks Hanksville and can be seen from the highway. We suggest off roading and getting closer to it as the landscape is just surreal 
🌒 Moon Overlook- Otherworldly landscape which looks so much like the surface of the Moon. Best accessed via a 4x4, this spot is located close to Hanksville

caption:
‼️A day in the Austrian Alps looks a little different when you stay somewhere like this👇🏻

I woke up with the mountains filling the windows, birds chirping, made tea and then some coffee + toast, and spent the morning relaxing by my private (and huge) infinity pool.

Eventually I got ready for my most important appointment of the day - meeting the horses that live on the property. One apple later, I had made a new best friend.

Then came a very necessary plate of Kaiserschmarrn, because I refuse to visit Austria and behave responsibly around Austrian desserts. The lovely family that owns the hotel, loves feeding and surprising the guests.

The afternoon was intentionally slow…back to my chalet for some quiet time, then the spa, sauna and lounge before heading to Huwi’s Alm for dinner.

And my favorite part might have been coming back afterward. Fireplace going, a sparkly drink, doors open to feel that crisp cold Alpine air before crawling into bed.

If you’re looking for a luxury chalet in Austria, a romantic stay surrounded by the Alps, a wellness focused vacation, a spa stay or a unique place to stay near Salzburg, save @priesteregg_premium_ecoresort for your Austria trip.

This is Saariselkä in Finnish Lapland, and it’s one of the places I’d choose specifically for aurora chasing.

You’re way up at around 68° north, right under the auroral zone, and unlike bigger cities, you can get away from light pollution really fast.

My biggest tip is that - don’t obsess over the KP number. In northern Lapland, you can still get beautiful and bright auroras on lower KP nights.

What you should check -
clear skies and cloud cover first
get away from streetlights
give yourself several nights, not just one
look for open sky around Kaunispää, Kiilopää or outside the village
stay out longer than you think because the sky can change FAST
this was right outside my hotel!

And if the forecast looks bad where you are, sometimes driving 20 to 30 minutes can put you under completely different cloud cover.

No place can guarantee the Northern Lights, but if they’re the main reason you’re coming to Lapland, Saariselkä gives you a very good setup to chase them.

caption:
‼️if you are visiting Venice this year👇🏻 

🤍 Follow for more unique places and travel guides around the world

Getting there

Fly into Venice Marco Polo Airport. From there, you can take a water taxi (expensive but iconic) or the Alilaguna water bus (budget-friendly). 

If you’re coming by train, Venezia Santa Lucia drops you straight into the heart of the city.

Where to stay

If it’s your first time, stay near San Marco or along the Grand Canal so you can walk everywhere early in the morning before crowds take over.

🤍 I stayed at the @stregisvenice and it was an epic experience. One of my favorite moments of staying here was that every evening they carry on a ritual called champagne sabering - where a bottle is opened with a sword (yes, an actual sword) and I actually got to do it myself and then try it 🤍

Things to do

Get lost. Not even kidding! Venice is best experienced with no plan
Wake up early and walk through Piazza San Marco before 8 AM
Take a vaporetto or gondola ride down the Grand Canal
Visit Burano for colorful houses or Murano for glassmaking
Climb the Campanile for one of the best views in the city

What to eat

Skip the tourist places right by the main squares.
Walk a few streets away and look for smaller, local spots.
Try cicchetti (Venetian tapas), fresh pasta, and tiramisu (this is where it was born).
Also, don’t leave without having a spritz by the water.

Things no one tells you ⚠️

Venice is beautiful, but it’s also crowded. Early mornings and late evenings are your best friend
Restaurants near major attractions are often overpriced and not worth it
Pack light! There are a LOT of bridges and no Ubers here
Acqua alta (flooding) can happen, especially in certain months, so check ahead

caption:
‼️if you are visiting Tromso, I highly recommend renting a car once you are done with the city because some of the best scenery is OUTSIDE the city 👇🏻

🤍 Follow @tripuntraveled for unique places, road trips and stays around the world.

Tromsø is incredible, but if you have a car, give yourself at least one or two days to explore beyond the city.

These are some of my favorite places to add to a winter road trip:

📍Kvaløya
Probably the easiest from Tromsø. There are huge snow-covered mountains, frozen-looking fjords, tiny red cabins and roads that keep getting prettier around every corner.

📍Grøtfjord
A tiny coastal village surrounded by mountains. In winter, the contrast between the dark Arctic water, white beach and completely snow-covered landscape is unreal.

📍Sommarøy
One of the most beautiful drives from Tromsø. Small islands, bridges, fishing villages and snowy mountains right beside the ocean.

📍Ersfjordbotn
An easy stop with views

📍Lyngen Alps
If you want the landscapes to feel even more dramatic, head toward Lyngen. Massive alpine peaks above the fjords and everything feels much more remote.

📍Senja
If you have more time, keep going. Senja deserves much more than a quick stop, but in winter the snowy fishing villages, winding coastal roads and huge mountains are some of the most dramatic scenery in Northern Norway.

🚗 My biggest tip is RENT A CAR if you can safely drive in snow

You can stop whenever the light looks good, explore tiny villages and actually experience the landscapes you came all the way to the Arctic to see.

And in winter, always check the weather + road conditions before heading out. Northern Norway can change very quickly.

Honestly, I came to Tromsø expecting the Northern Lights to be the highlight.

The drives outside the city ended up being just as memorable with some of the most insane northern lights visible to the naked eye. I have seen bright greens, purple, pink, red…

caption:
‼️Everyone tells you what to pack for Lapland. Nobody tells you what NOT to pack

🤍 follow for unique places, roadtrips, and winter destinations around the world @tripuntraveled 

DON’T pack extra-thick everything - secret to surviving Lapland isn’t wearing the thickest clothes you can find. It’s leaving enough room to layer properly for insulation . This includes your boots.

A different outfit for every day - Lapland is one of the easiest places to repeat outfits because 90% of your photos show your outerwear only anyway.

Your own snowmobile/ski/snowshoe gear unless you specifically need it. Most of this is easily rented, and many guided activities already provide Arctic clothing. Check your bookings first.

Thin touchscreen gloves as your only gloves. Bring them as liners if you want, but for standing outside watching the Northern Lights, proper mittens are a must.

Cotton thermals - This is the surprising one I’d emphasize. Don’t make cotton your base layer. Bring merino wool or a good moisture-wicking synthetic layer instead. 

Leave the cute boots that have no insulation or grip at home. Snow boots should actually be warm, waterproof and roomy enough for wool socks.

✅ What SHOULD you pack?
Merino base layers, wool socks, a balaclava, a proper beanie and layers. It’s not about wearing more clothes…it’s about wearing the right ones

Follow @tripuntraveled for more unique places, winter destinations and road trips around the world.

If your dream vacation looks like a Christmas movie, this place needs to be on your winter list

this city in winter that feels completely unreal…and I keep going back…
snow falling under glowing streetlights,
colorful wooden houses,
mountains straight behind the city and 
long blue Arctic evenings where everything feels a little more magical

It’s one of the best winter bases in Northern Norway for combining a city with Arctic experiences.

A few things I’d recommend
❄️ Walk around the city center while it’s snowing
🏔️ Take the Fjellheisen cable car for the view over Tromsø and the surrounding islands
🌌 Go looking for the Northern Lights away from the city lights
🚗 Road trip around Kvaløya and the fjords outside Tromsø
🌊 Drive toward Sommarøy for some of the prettiest Arctic scenery around the city

and if you visit during polar night season, don’t expect complete darkness all day.

You can get hours of gorgeous soft blue and pink twilight.
